output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Plausible values: keep the scoring basis with the draws}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mfrmr)
```

One posterior mean gives one summary per Person. Repeated posterior draws
retain variation around that summary and can be useful in later analyses.
The draws must travel with their IDs, scoring basis and limitations: exporting
numbers alone does not establish a valid population analysis.

This short example starts from the package's saved synthetic JML calibration,
scores two invented Persons, and saves the resulting object. It demonstrates
**conditional posterior scoring and data handoff**, not a survey regression or
a population-level uncertainty guarantee. No external survey package is needed.

## Draw values from a stated scoring model

<details>
<summary>Show R code: load the calibration and score two new Persons</summary>

```{r draw-values, results='hide'}
library(mfrmr)
example <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example$fit
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data(example$dataset)

# Invented responses using levels present in the saved calibration.
new_ratings <- data.frame(
  Person = rep(c("NEW01", "NEW02"), each = 2),
  Rater = as.character(unique(ratings$Rater)[1]),
  Criterion = rep(as.character(unique(ratings$Criterion)[1:2]), 2),
  Score = c(2, 3, 1, 2)
)
pv <- sample_mfrm_plausible_values(
  fit, new_ratings, n_draws = 20, seed = 23
)
```

</details>

The source fit is JML. This scoring step adds the package's standard-normal
reference prior while keeping the fitted facet/step calibration fixed. The
prior is an assumption for posterior scoring; JML has not estimated a Person
population distribution. For supported MML fits, the default instead uses the
fitted population, including Person covariates when specified.

```{r draw-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(pv$values[c("Person", "Draw", "Value", "CalibrationMethod")]),
             digits = 3)
```

The same Person appears once per draw. Twenty draws do not turn two Persons
into forty independent observations. Values are sampled from the fitted
quadrature-grid posterior; repetitions of a value are expected.

## Inspect the numerical review and retain its meaning

<details>
<summary>Show R code: inspect summaries, settings and review information</summary>

```{r inspect-values, results='hide'}
draw_summary <- summary(pv)$draw_summary
draw_summary[c("Person", "Draws", "MeanValue", "SDValue")]
pv$settings[c("method", "posterior_basis", "scoring_quad_points", "seed")]
pv$row_review
pv$population_review
pv$notes
```

</details>

```{r summary-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(draw_summary[c("Person", "Draws", "MeanValue", "SDValue")],
             digits = 3)
```

These are summaries of a finite set of draws. With twenty draws, the empirical
mean, SD and quantiles have appreciable Monte Carlo variation. The companion
`pv$estimates` table contains the posterior scoring summaries computed from the
quadrature rule. Increasing the number of draws can reduce simulation error;
it does not supply missing conditioning variables or calibration uncertainty.

## Save the complete object before reshaping

<details>
<summary>Show R code: save, reload and split into one table per draw</summary>

```{r save-values, eval=FALSE}
# Choose a private location for real Person data.
local_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mfrmr-pv-example")
dir.create(local_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(pv, file.path(local_dir, "plausible-values.rds"))
restored <- readRDS(file.path(local_dir, "plausible-values.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(pv, restored))

by_draw <- split(restored$values, restored$values$Draw)
stopifnot(all(vapply(by_draw, function(x) !anyDuplicated(x$Person), logical(1))))
```

</details>

The RDS retains the scoring settings, fit identity, review tables and notes.
Each `by_draw` table can be joined to a Person-level background/design table by
ID for a downstream analysis. Check missing, duplicate and unmatched IDs before
joining. Keep the full object even if a receiving tool needs a wide matrix or
a smaller set of columns. For an analysis bundle with its source fit, see
[`export_mfrm_bundle()`](../reference/export_mfrm_bundle.html).

## Choose the downstream analysis separately

| Intended use | What remains to justify |
| --- | --- |
| Describe these conditional draws | Their scoring prior, calibration, numerical review and finite-draw approximation. |
| Estimate a population mean or regression | A conditioning model compatible with that analysis, the target population, sampling design and an appropriate uncertainty-combination rule. The two-Person example does not establish these. |
| Use official IEA plausible values | Follow that survey's PV and sampling documentation directly; no mfrmr recalibration is required. |

[BIFIEsurvey's data interface](https://konradoberwimmer.github.io/BIFIEsurvey/reference/BIFIE.data.html)
and [EdSurvey's survey objects](https://american-institutes-for-research.github.io/EdSurvey/reference/edsurvey-class.html)
are possible downstream routes. This page does not claim a tested adapter to
either package. Use their documented analysis workflow when it matches the
question, and verify the within-PV, between-PV and combined variance for that
workflow. Rating weights, sampling weights and replicate weights have distinct
roles. An ordinary regression on averaged PVs or on all draws stacked as
independent people does not perform that uncertainty propagation.

Calibration and fitted population parameters remain fixed in the current
draws. A downstream variance calculation does not automatically add their
estimation uncertainty. See
[`sample_mfrm_plausible_values()`](../reference/sample_mfrm_plausible_values.html)
for supported models and scoring options. Independent downstream code can use
these outputs without a new mfrmr API or an IEA-specific workflow.
